info.bio:
Gram Parsons y Chris Hilmann miembros de The Byrds con Sneaky Pete Kleinow y Chris Ethridge  formarán en la década de los 70 el embrión del mítico grupo que será la base y fuente de otros posteriores como los Eagles.
Mas adelante ingresarán en Burrito otros músicos como Gene Parsons o Bernie Leadon que irán conformando la leyenda dal grupo pionero y mas importante de la música country rock.

scenes.name: Country-rock y roots-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: En los setenta, el reajuste a los viejos valores (blues, folk, country) convierte al rock en uno de los mayores éxitos del consumismo: el Establishment ya no intenta destruirlo, lo absorbe. El country-rock de Gram Parsons es una moda enorme: Commander Cody, New Riders Of The Purple Sage, Manassas, Nitty Gritty Dirt Band, Poco y los Eagles (Desperado, Hotel California); en Nashville surgen los «outlaws» (Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson, Kris Kristofferson). El roots-rock sigue con Hot Tuna, Little Feat y Doobie Brothers, y la nostalgia recupera el blues (Roy Buchanan, Bonnie Raitt), la armonía vocal (Manhattan Transfer, Roches, McGarrigle Sisters) y los cincuenta (American Graffiti).

podcast.title: Country Rock Pioneers (1968)
podcast.body: Formed in Southern California in 1968 by former Byrds members Chris Hillman and Gram Parsons, The Flying Burrito Brothers are recognized as pioneers of country rock. Their musical "DNA" significantly influenced later bands such as the Eagles and Firefall. "The Flying Burrito Brothers, a band that was formed by former members of the birds, Chris Hillman and Graham Parsons in Southern California in 1968 are country rock pioneers."

podcast.title: Festival Express Participants
podcast.body: The Flying Burrito Brothers were among the notable musicians and bands participating in the Festival Express traveling rock festival in the summer of 1970. "How about Janice Joplin, the Great Bull Zed, the band, traffic, buddy guy, Delaney and Bonnie, the flying burrito brothers."

podcast.title: Hay Publicity Stunt
podcast.body: For the release party of "Gilded Palace of Sin," attendees received packages of hay as a publicity stunt intended to signal the album's country influences. The United States Postal Service even tested the hay to determine if it might be marijuana. This creative marketing generated significant media buzz and established the band's image as "psychedelic cow punks" who were "drug-addled." "If you got an invitation to the release party for the Gilded Palace of Sin, you also got a package of hay."

podcast.title: Influence on Tom Petty
podcast.body: Tom Petty considered his band, The Heartbreakers, to be in the tradition of The Flying Burrito Brothers, a California band, influencing his decision to move to Los Angeles and shaping the musical identity of his group. "he made it clear that he considered the heartbreakers to be a california band in the tradition of buffalo springfield the flying burrito brothers and even the beach boys and that's why."

podcast.title: Musical Influence on The Eagles
podcast.body: Glenn Frey acknowledged that The Eagles borrowed "a bit from the Burrito Brothers," specifically their "toughness," although he noted they "weren't that good a band vocally." "the burrito brothers had the toughness but they weren't that good a band vocally so we kind of wanted to combine both of those elements."

podcast.title: Passing the Torch to The Eagles
podcast.body: Chris Hillman stated that The Flying Burrito Brothers "handed the ball off to the Eagles," implying their pioneering role in country rock paved the way for The Eagles' success. "Chris Hillman said that the flying burrito brothers handed the ball off to the eagles and they ran it in pretend touchdowns."

podcast.title: The Troubadour as Headquarters
podcast.body: The Flying Burrito Brothers regularly played at The Troubadour in Los Angeles, a club recognized as the "headquarters" and "ground zero" for country rock experimentation in Southern California during the 1970s. This venue was a crucial proving ground for the genre. "Hillman said was a regular in the crowd at the Trubidor in Los Angeles where the burritos played."
